title: Arrays Share a Common Element
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, return true if they share at least one common element.
mnemonic: Store one side, test the other
think: What is the task asking? Check whether the arrays intersect at least once.
What is the key operation? Fast membership check.
What wording signals stand out? Common element, share at least one, intersection.
What is the brute force idea? Compare every element of nums1 with every element of nums2.
What is the better/optimal idea? Put one array in a set and scan the other.
What are the edge cases? Empty arrays, duplicates, negative numbers.
What is the complexity? O(n + m) time and O(n) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I store the first array in a set and check whether any element from the second array exists in it.
algorithm: If current element exists in set -> return true
interview: I would use a HashSet for fast membership checks. I store one array and scan the other until I find an overlap.
ru: Кладём элементы первого массива в set и смотрим, встречается ли хоть один элемент второго массива в этом set.

critical: Use nested loops without noticing set lookup
important: Build set from wrong side and still do extra work
nice: Do not mention O(n + m) time

gaps: Nice to have: explain why duplicates in input do not matter
whyThisPattern: This is a HashSet problem because the core operation is fast existence checking.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because counts are irrelevant.
Not Two Pointers, because arrays are not sorted and no inward movement is needed.
